Rugby-Inspired Wales beat New Zealand for first time in 73 years Reuters | Updated: 14-11-2026 21:42 IST | Created: 14-11-2026 21:42 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Wales pulled off one of rugby’s biggest upsets, ending a 73-year winless sequence against New Zealand to beat the All Blacks 35-28 in the Nations Championship on Saturday. They outscored the visitors five tries to four to end a 34-match winning streak for New Zealand in fixtures between the teams. Wales last won against the All Blacks in 1953 and have slumped to some of their worst results in recent years but produced a defensive performance for the ages to shade the Kiwis. They caught the visitors cold with two early tries and two more at the start of the second half, and heroic Welsh defence resisted waves of New Zealand attacks in the closing stages to hold on for a famous victory. (Writing by Mark Gleeson in Cape Town; Editing by Ed Osmond)

item.content:encoded:
European shares end best week since June as strong earnings lift sentiment Reuters | Updated: 13-11-2026 23:16 IST | Created: 13-11-2026 23:16 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

European shares were little changed on Friday, but recorded their best week since late June as strong earnings and a rotation out of tech globally helped investors look past geopolitical risks and the volatility involving AI stocks. The STOXX 600 closed flat at 664.14 points, and gained over 2% for the week. Heavyweight Euro STOXX banks index rose over 4% this week and led broader gains. Robust earnings, along with a fall in oil prices on hopes of a potential easing of the US-Iran conflict earlier this week, helped the STOXX 600 breach record-high levels for the first time since August on Thursday. Analysts also pointed to structural tailwinds that could boost Europe's prospects in the long term. "Europe is building its rearmament program, its industrial program, strategic autonomy, its energy infrastructure and its defence," said Jitania Kandhari, deputy CIO, Solutions & Multi-Assets at Morgan Stanley Investment Management. "That is trickling into different pockets of the economy and the markets now. When investment in capex picks up, it has spillover effects," she said. Mirroring the optimism, Goldman Sachs raised its 12-month target for the STOXX 600 to 700 points from 695. TECH LOSES STEAM On Friday, the tech sector fell 1.3%, leading losses. Uncertainty over the outlook for the AI trade rippled through global markets following Jensen Huang's abrupt resignation as Nvidia's CEO, as investors fretted about the future of the AI goliath that has underpinned much of the rally in global markets. Chip stocks such as Infineon and Aixtron were down more than 4% each, while AI equipment makers such as Schneider Electric and Legrand were also lower. Adding to caution, crude prices swung in the session as Washington's focus on blockading Iran and ramping up other economic pressures allayed fears of renewed direct conflict in the Middle East. Investors also weighed some corporate earnings on Friday. Wise Group gained 7.7% to top the benchmark index after the money transfer company reported a 23% net revenue rise in the first half of its fiscal year. In contrast, Richemont fell 3.8% after the Cartier owner reported weaker-than-expected sales in its jewellery unit during the second quarter. Acciona fell 8%, languishing at the bottom of the index after subsidiary Acciona Energia said it would not meet its €2 billion ($2.21 billion) target for its asset rotation programme. On the data front, the euro zone economy grew by 0.4% quarter-on-quarter in the third quarter, according to a flash gross domestic product estimate from the EU's statistics agency. ($1 = 0.9065 euros)

item.description: Polish President Karol Nawrocki vetoed legislation on Friday that would have let regulators decide whether online content is illegal and order it blocked, his second rejection of a bill ...
item.content:encoded:
Polish President Nawrocki vetoes digital content bill for second time Reuters | Updated: 13-11-2026 22:48 IST | Created: 13-11-2026 22:48 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Polish President Karol Nawrocki vetoed legislation on Friday that would have let regulators decide whether online content is illegal and order it blocked, his second rejection of a bill implementing the European Union’s Digital Services Act. Nawrocki said the bill, which had been narrowed and resubmitted after he vetoed an earlier version in January, gave state officials excessive power over online speech. "It is not the role of an official to rule on whether a given piece of content constitutes a crime or not. That is solely the role of independent courts," he said in a video on X. The bill, which the Sejm, the lower house of parliament, passed in October, would have let regulators order the blocking of online content including criminal threats and incitement to violence, with appeals routed through courts. Nawrocki, an ally of the nationalist opposition, and Prime Minister Donald Tusk's pro-European coalition government have clashed repeatedly since he took office, as the president has vetoed 48 of the government's bills. The legislation had gained urgency after a string of knife attacks at Polish schools in October, including one in which a 15-year-old wore a helmet-mounted camera and appeared to intend to film the attack. Digital Affairs Minister Krzysztof Gawkowski said the veto would leave Poland without the tools the government says are needed to respond quickly to such cases. "This veto is not just throwing legislation in the trash — it’s permission for hate, hatred and the death that the internet also brings," Gawkowski said in a post on X. Nawrocki rejected the link between the bill and the school attacks, accusing the government of exploiting the violence to push the legislation through. "They exploited a tragedy, applied emotional blackmail, to push through regulations that give the government essentially arbitrary control and the ability to decide what we can and cannot say, write or publish," he said. Tusk defended the bill in a post on X. "Protecting children from online criminals. It is hard to imagine a more important issue that should unite people across political divides. And yet he vetoed it," Tusk said. Gawkowski told a press conference he would draft another bill on the issue.

item.content:encoded:
Taiwan accuses China of pressuring Papua New Guinea to expel Taiwanese diplomats During a legislative hearing on Thursday, Lin Hung-hsun, Deputy Director-General of Taiwan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs Department of East Asian and Pacific Affairs, said PNG initially demanded the closure of Taiwan's representative office on July 16, citing its adherence to the "one-China" policy. ANI | Updated: 13-11-2026 21:53 IST | Created: 13-11-2026 21:53 IST

Representative Image (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Taiwan has accused China of pressuring Papua New Guinea (PNG) to expel Taiwanese diplomats and shut down its representative office in Port Moresby, alleging that Beijing may have used economic incentives to influence the Pacific nation's sudden diplomatic decision, according to a report by Central News Agency (CNA). During a legislative hearing on Thursday, Lin Hung-hsun, Deputy Director-General of Taiwan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs Department of East Asian and Pacific Affairs, said PNG initially demanded the closure of Taiwan's representative office on July 16, citing its adherence to the "one-China" policy. According to CNA, Taiwan and PNG subsequently held discussions and reached an understanding that PNG would provide one year's written notice before the representative office was closed. However, on November 6, PNG reportedly reversed its earlier position and demanded that Taiwanese diplomats leave the country within seven days. Deputy Foreign Minister Chen Ming-chi told lawmakers that Taiwan believed the sudden change in PNG's position was driven by pressure from Beijing. He pointed to a recent visit by a high-level PNG delegation to China and the upcoming visit of PNG Prime Minister James Marape to China to attend the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit. "Given these circumstances, our assessment is that the government of Papua New Guinea may have been subjected to significant pressure from China or even offered economic incentives," Chen said, as cited by CNA. Chen also highlighted China's announcement that it was prepared to increase imports of liquefied natural gas (LNG) from PNG. This came after Taiwan decided to stop purchasing LNG from the Pacific nation following its demand to close the Taiwanese representative office. The diplomatic dispute concerns the Taiwan Economic Office, which was established in Port Moresby in 1990. On November 6, PNG's Department of Foreign Affairs announced that its secretary, Elias Wohengu, had instructed the office's head, Chiu Chen-yu, and First Secretary Lee Chung-nun to leave the country within seven days. The remaining diplomat, Pan Shao-jyun, was permitted to stay to oversee the office's closure within a year. PNG's foreign affairs department also clarified that although Taiwan had been given 12 months to complete the closure, this should not be interpreted as a guarantee that existing staffing and operational arrangements would remain unchanged during that period. In response, Taiwan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) announced that it would shut down the representative office and withdraw all personnel stationed in PNG. The ministry also said it would conduct a comprehensive review and adjustment of its relations with PNG, taking into account Taiwan's national dignity, diplomatic autonomy and overall national interests. According to CNA, Taiwan has since begun withdrawing its diplomatic and technical mission personnel from the Pacific nation. PNG maintains diplomatic relations with China, which follows a policy of not allowing its diplomatic allies to maintain simultaneous official diplomatic relations with Taiwan. The latest developments have further highlighted Beijing's diplomatic pressure on countries maintaining or considering engagement with Taipei. (ANI)
